title: String Formatter Functions
story: Your social media posts look boring — all lowercase, no excitement. You need a set of text-transforming tools to title-case your headlines, add exclamation marks, and repeat catchy words for emphasis.
why: String manipulation functions show how input text can be transformed through a pipeline of operations — a pattern used everywhere from web apps to compilers.
analogy: String formatting is like a photo editing app with filters. You apply the 'uppercase' filter, then the 'add excitement' filter, then the 'repeat' filter. Each filter transforms the image (string) and hands it to the next filter in the pipeline.
try_it: Write a `reverse_text(text: Str) -> Str` function that reverses a string using a while loop, and add it to the formatting pipeline before `add_exclamation`.
tips: string.str_upper and string.str_lower transform the entire string
Use `+` to concatenate two strings simply; use string.str_concat in loops
Build pipelines by assigning each function's output to a new variable
A while loop inside a function lets you repeat operations a variable number of times
common_mistakes: Forgetting to initialize the result variable as an empty string `""` before the loop
Not incrementing the counter in the while loop — causes infinite loop
Confusing string.str_upper (entire string) with capitalizing just the first letter
